title: Onboarding's 'Regulated cooling' toggle never enables cooling; the camera runs at ambient every session
what_happened: Onboarding step 9 'Set your capture defaults' has a 'Regulated cooling' switch ('Turn on for a cooled camera; leave off for a DSLR or an uncooled sensor'). I turned it ON and it revealed 'Cooling set-point -10 C'. The saved profile has default_cooling_temp=-10.0 but cool_on_connect=0. On every connect the camera sat at 20.0 C with the cooler at 0%, and the app log shows it polling and doing nothing: '[CameraTemperaturePoller] Camera temp: 20.0C, power: 0%, target: -10.0C'. The connect sequence issues camera_set_gain and camera_set_offset but no cooling command at all. The manual 'Cool to -10C' button works (reaches -10.0 C / 35% within ~50 s), and ticking the hidden 'Cool on connect' checkbox inside Equipment > Edit Profile > Camera Defaults makes the camera cool automatically on the next Connect All -- so the feature works; only the wizard fails to wire it. There is also no cooling control anywhere in Settings: searching Settings for 'cool' returns 'No settings match your search', while app_settings holds cooling_behavior='On Connect' with no UI and no effect.
expected: Turning on 'Regulated cooling' with a set-point in the wizard should set cool_on_connect=1 so the camera actually reaches the set-point when it connects. Otherwise the switch is decorative and a first-run user images all night on a warm sensor.
repro: 1. Fresh profile, walk onboarding, step 9: turn 'Regulated cooling' ON, leave set-point -10. Save profile. 2. sqlite3 <db> 'select cool_on_connect,default_cooling_temp from equipment_profiles' -> 0 | -10.0. 3. Equipment > Connect All. Camera card shows 20.0 C / 0% / Idle indefinitely. 4. Equipment > Edit Profile > Camera Defaults > tick 'Cool on connect' > Save. 5. Disconnect All, Connect All -> camera card shows -10.0 C / 35%.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-cool.png (wizard toggle ON + set-point -10), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-camcard3.png (20.0C/0% after reconnect), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-ep5.png ('Cool on connect' unchecked in Edit Profile), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-cool4.png (-10.0C/35% after enabling it), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-searchcool.png ('No settings match your search' for 'cool'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/dumplog.txt line 'Camera temp: 20.0C, power: 0%, target: -10.0C'
proposed_fix: Map the wizard's 'Regulated cooling' switch to cool_on_connect (and keep default_cooling_temp for the set-point). Also either surface or delete the orphaned app_settings key cooling_behavior='On Connect', which has no UI and no effect.
verdict_reasoning: The factual core is confirmed in code but the finding's framing is over-called. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/onboarding_provider.dart:429 hardcodes coolOnConnect: false, with an explicit 8-line comment stating this is deliberate ('we never auto-run the TEC on connect just because a set-point exists: a setup done in the middle of a summer day must not pin the cooler at full power for hours'). The wizard control (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/onboarding/steps/camera_defaults_step.dart:359-361) is labelled 'Regulated cooling / Turn on for a cooled camera; leave off for a DSLR or an uncooled sensor' -- it is a camera-capability question, it never promises cool-on-connect, and it is not decorative: it gates and persists default_cooling_temp. So 'the toggle never enables cooling' is true only against an expectation the UI does not set. The orphan-setting sub-claim IS fully confirmed and is the real defect here: 'cooling_behavior' defaults to 'On Connect' (database/default_settings.dart:55), is round-tripped through every settings mapper, has zero consumers that act on it (grep across packages/ and apps/ excluding generated files finds only storage/mapping), and has no UI -- I reproduced 'No settings match your search' for 'cool' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-22-searchcool.png). Severity P1 -> P3.

title: 'Connect All result' strip keeps claiming devices are Connected after they have been disconnected
what_happened: After Connect All, a persistent strip sits under the header reading 'Connect All result | camera Connected | mount Connected | focuser Connected | filter wheel Connected | Clear'. I then disconnected the camera: its card vanished, the header pill correctly changed to '3 connected' and the status bar to '3/4 | Camera Disconnected' -- but the strip still showed a green 'camera Connected'. Worse, after Disconnect All the strip still showed all four green 'Connected' chips while the main area said 'No devices connected' and the pill said 0/4. On the next launch the same strip is relabelled 'Startup auto-connect result' and behaves the same way.
expected: Either clear/update the strip when connection state changes, or label it unambiguously as a historical record with a timestamp ('Connect All at 11:16: 4 of 4 succeeded') so a green 'Connected' chip is never read as current state.
repro: 1. Equipment > Connect All (strip appears, 4 green chips). 2. Click the disconnect icon on the camera card > 'Disconnect anyway'. 3. Strip still shows 'camera Connected' while the pill reads '3 connected'. 4. Disconnect All -> strip still shows all four Connected next to 'No devices connected'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-camdisc.png (camera card gone, strip still 'camera Connected'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-80-coolonconnect.png ('No devices connected' + 0/4 with four green Connected chips), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-pill.png ('3 connected'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-sb2.png ('3/4 Camera Disconnected')
proposed_fix: Re-render the strip from live device state, or freeze it as a timestamped result banner that visually cannot be confused with the live status chips.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly: after Disconnect All the strip still showed four green chips 'camera/mount/focuser/filter wheel Connected' while the main area read 'No devices connected' and the profile card read 0/4 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-09-disc.png); on the next launch the same strip was relabelled 'Startup auto-connect result' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-35-equip3.png). This is by design and documented: equipment_screen/progress_dashboard.dart:10-14 -- 'After a sweep completes the chips remain visible until clear() is called, so the user can review what failed without having to re-run Connect All' -- and the widget renders purely from the deviceConnectionProgressProvider snapshot with no live device state. Severity P2 -> P3: the strip is already labelled with a past-tense '<source> result' and carries a Clear button, and the live pill/status bar/profile card all disagree with it visibly on the same screen; the real gap is the missing timestamp and the identical chip styling.

title: First Light 'Retry' button never re-runs the query
what_happened: The First Light candidate list failed to load and rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-1 / ^' with a 'Retry' button. I corrected the underlying row in the database, then clicked Retry three times over several minutes: the identical error re-rendered every time, still quoting the old value 'tile-1' that no longer exists in the database. Restarting the app made the list load correctly and render the candidate, proving the data was fine and Retry simply never re-executed the query. Separately, this error state leaks a raw Dart exception (class name and caret diagram) straight into the user-facing UI.
expected: Retry must invalidate and re-run the provider. The error surface should show a human message plus a copyable detail, not a raw FormatException with a caret.
repro: 1. Put a row in transient_detections whose tile_id cannot be parsed as an int. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light -> error state. 3. Fix the row in the DB. 4. Click Retry repeatedly -> same error, same stale value. 5. Restart the app -> loads fine.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-104-firstlight.png (error), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-105-fl2.png (identical after DB fix + Retry), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-106-fl3.png (loads after restart with the same data)
proposed_fix: Have Retry call ref.invalidate on the candidates provider. Wrap the error in a user-facing message and keep the exception behind a 'details' expander.
verdict_reasoning: Symptom reproduced exactly: seeded transient_detections.tile_id = 'tile-1' (TEXT), First Light rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-1 / ^' with the raw Dart exception and caret leaking into the UI; I then corrected the row to 7 and clicked Retry three times -- identical error, still quoting 'tile-1' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-49-flerror2.png, eqv-51-retry3.png). BUT the stated cause is wrong and the proposed fix is already in the code: first_light_view.dart:409 is literally onPressed: () => ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider). The actual mechanism is that firstLightCandidatesProvider (transient_detections_provider.dart:138-150) is a StreamProvider over a drift select().watch() (transient_detections_dao.dart:73-78); drift's cached query stream replays its last snapshot -- here an error -- to the new subscriber instead of re-executing, so invalidate cannot clear it. Important caveat that halves the severity: both my repro and the reporter's corrected the row with an out-of-band sqlite3 write, which drift by design cannot observe; an in-app (drift) write to that table would push a fresh snapshot and recover the view. Severity P2 -> P3. The raw-exception-in-UI sub-claim is fully confirmed and is the part worth fixing outright.

title: The delete-profile confirmation says 'This cannot be undone' and then offers a working Undo
what_happened: Right-click a profile > Delete raises 'Delete Profile / Delete "My First Rig"? This cannot be undone.' Confirming produces a snackbar with an Undo action, and Undo genuinely restores the profile in full: after undoing the deletion of my only profile the row came back with name, focal_length 550.0, filter_names ["LumTest","R","G","B","Ha","OIII","SII"], default_gain 100, cool_on_connect 1, is_default 1, is_active 1.
expected: Say what is true: either drop the 'cannot be undone' sentence and mention the undo window, or remove the Undo.
repro: 1. Equipment > right-click profile > Delete. 2. Read 'This cannot be undone.' 3. Confirm. 4. Click Undo in the snackbar. 5. sqlite3 <db> 'select * from equipment_profiles' -> profile fully restored.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-delconf.png ('This cannot be undone.'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-118-noprofiles2.png (Undo snackbar), post-undo DB row shown above
proposed_fix: Change the copy to 'Delete "<name>"? You can undo this for a few seconds.'
verdict_reasoning: Copy verified verbatim at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/widgets/profile_sidebar.dart:432 ('Delete "${profile.name}"? This cannot be undone.') and live (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-39-delconf.png), and confirming raises a snackbar carrying an Undo SnackBarAction (equipment_screen.dart:437-457) wired to _restoreDeletedProfile with a full versioned JSON export taken before the delete. One correction that makes it worse, not better, than reported: in my run the Undo did NOT restore -- I had navigated Equipment -> Dashboard first, and _restoreDeletedProfile is a State method guarded by mounted/_isCurrentProfileOperation, so it aborted silently with no feedback and the row stayed deleted. So the dialog says 'cannot be undone', then offers an Undo, and that Undo is silently unreliable once you leave the screen. Severity P3 stands for the copy defect.

title: Two profiles can share the same name, making the delete confirmation genuinely ambiguous
what_happened: The New Profile dialog validates an empty name ('Fix 1 problem before saving - Profile name is required') but accepts a name identical to an existing profile. I created a second profile also called 'My First Rig'; the sidebar then showed two entries distinguishable only by their subtitle ('Sky-Watcher Esprit 100ED + Sim...' vs '0 devices'), the screen header, the status bar and the Delete confirmation all just say 'My First Rig'. The delete dialog reading 'Delete "My First Rig"? This cannot be undone.' cannot tell the user which of the two is about to be destroyed. The second profile also saved with no devices and focal_length 0.0 with no warning.
expected: Reject or auto-suffix duplicate profile names, and include a disambiguator (devices/telescope) in the delete confirmation.
repro: 1. Equipment > '+' > name it exactly the same as an existing profile > Save Changes. 2. sqlite3 <db> 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' -> two rows, same name. 3. Right-click either > Delete: the dialog quotes only the shared name.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-84-dupname.png (two identical entries), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-del.png (ambiguous confirmation), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-emptyname.png (empty-name validation that does work)
proposed_fix: Add a uniqueness check to the same validator that already catches the empty name, or append ' (2)'.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: created a second profile named exactly 'My First Rig'; the DB now holds id 1 and id 2 with identical names (second saved with focal_length 0.0 and no devices, no warning), the sidebar shows two entries distinguishable only by subtitle ('Sky-Watcher Esprit 100ED + Sim...' vs '0 devices') (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-37-dupname.png), and the delete dialog quotes only 'Delete "My First Rig"? This cannot be undone.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-39-delconf.png). Code confirms the gap: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/equipment_profile_validation.dart:95 is the only name check and it rejects nothing but empty; there is no uniqueness constraint on equipment_profiles.name (only a non-unique idx_profiles_name index). Severity P3 stands.

title: Transient alert popover reports a -2.35 delta-mag brightening as 'mag 2.4'
what_happened: A detection with delta_mag = -2.35 (a 2.35-magnitude brightening) renders in the title-bar notification popover as 'NS J0.71+41.3 / Other / mag 2.4 / NEW'. The candidate card itself correctly shows '-2.35 mag' with an up-arrow, so the two surfaces disagree. 'mag 2.4' reads as an apparent magnitude of 2.4 -- a naked-eye star -- not as a delta. The designation 'NS J0.71+41.3' also encodes RA in hours rather than the IAU JHHMMSS.s+DDMMSS form the TNS expects, for a feature whose stated purpose is TNS submission.
expected: Show the signed delta with its symbol, e.g. 'delta-mag -2.35', matching the card. Use an IAU-form designation (this object is J004244.30+411607.3).
repro: 1. Have a transient_detections row with delta_mag = -2.35, ra_deg 10.6847, dec_deg 41.2687. 2. Click the bell in the title bar. 3. Popover reads 'NS J0.71+41.3 ... mag 2.4'. 4. Compare with the card in Analytics > Science > First Light, which reads '-2.35 mag'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-119-bell.png (popover 'mag 2.4'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-106-fl3.png (card '-2.35 mag'); the card's RA/Dec formatting is correct (00h 42m 44.3s +41 16' 7.3")
where: transient alert popover formatter and the designation builder feeding it
proposed_fix: Format delta magnitudes with sign and a delta label everywhere, and build designations from the sexagesimal RA/Dec the card already computes correctly.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with the reporter's exact numbers. Seeded delta_mag = -2.35 at ra_deg 10.6847 / dec_deg 41.2687; the bell popover reads 'NS J0.71+41.3 / Other / mag 2.4 / NEW' while the First Light card for the same row reads '-2.35 mag' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-20-bell.png vs eqv-18-dipole.png). A second seeded row (-1.72) renders 'NS J13.50+47.2 ... mag 1.7'. Code: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 sets magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs() (sign discarded, then rendered under an apparent-magnitude label), and _provisionalName (62-68) builds 'NS J' + RA in HOURS to 2dp + sign + |dec| in degrees to 1dp -- not the IAU JHHMMSS.s+DDMMSS form the TNS expects, even though the card computes the correct sexagesimal (00h 42m 44.3s +41 16' 7.3"). Severity P3 stands.

title: 'Connect All' silently connects a safety monitor that is not in the profile, and did not do so on an identical earlier click
what_happened: The 'Connect All' button lives under the profile card in the profile sidebar, so it reads as 'connect this profile's devices'. The first press (15:11:28 UTC) connected exactly the four profile devices. A second, identical press five minutes later (15:16:32) connected the same four plus sim_safety_monitor_1, which is not assigned to the profile -- the header pill changed to '5 connected - 1 unsaved' while the profile card and status bar both still said 4/4. The only thing that changed in between was that I had expanded the Discovery panel, which re-ran discovery. The device card does carry an honest note ('This session only -- not saved to your profile, so it will not reconnect next launch. Use Assign in Discovery to keep it.'), but the same button producing different results on two identical presses is the problem.
expected: Connect All should have one defined scope. If it deliberately picks up safety monitors, do it consistently and label the button accordingly ('Connect profile + safety'); otherwise restrict it to the profile.
repro: 1. Equipment > Connect All (log shows 4 connects). 2. Expand the Discovery panel (discovery re-runs). 3. Disconnect All, then Connect All again -> the log now also shows 'Connecting to Safety Monitor device: sim_safety_monitor_1' and the pill reads '5 connected - 1 unsaved'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-63-rednight-eq.png (safety monitor card + '5 connected - 1 unsaved' with profile still 4/4); app log 15:11:28 connects camera/focuser/mount/filterwheel only, 15:16:32 connects those four plus sim_safety_monitor_1
proposed_fix: Make the connect-all set deterministic from the profile (plus an explicit, documented safety-device rule) rather than from whatever the last discovery happened to cache.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: Connect All on a 4-device profile produced the pill '5 connected - 1 unsaved' with the profile card still 4/4 and a Simulated Safety Monitor card carrying the 'This session only - not saved to your profile' note (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-11-connectall.png); the app log shows 'Connecting to Safety Monitor device: sim_safety_monitor_1'. Cause found (the finding's file path is wrong -- there is no screens/equipment/command_handlers.dart): packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/equipment_screen.dart:659-700, immediately after the profile sweep, best-efforts a connect to unifiedSafetyMonitorsProvider.first when no safety monitor is connected. Because that provider is fed by the discovery cache, the outcome genuinely differs between two identical presses depending on whether discovery has run -- which is exactly the non-determinism reported. The profile sweep itself (device_service/profile_connections.dart:146-180) is correctly profile-scoped. Severity P3 stands.

title: The onboarding wizard's filter step lets you invent slots the wheel does not have
what_happened: After selecting the Simulated Filter Wheel the step listed its real 7 slots (L, R, G, B, Ha, OIII, SII). Pressing 'Add slot' immediately created an 8th row pre-filled 'Filter 8' with no warning that the connected wheel only reports 7 positions. Deleting a slot is also unconfirmed and renumbers everything below it, which would silently re-map per-filter focus offsets.
expected: Cap the slot count at what the wheel reports (or warn clearly that slot 8 does not exist on this wheel), and warn that deleting a middle slot renumbers the ones below it.
repro: 1. Onboarding step 6, select the Simulated Filter Wheel (7 slots appear). 2. Click 'Add slot' -> row 8 'Filter 8' appears with no warning.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-fw2.png (8 rows on a 7-position wheel), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-fw.png (the wheel's real 7 slots)
proposed_fix: Disable 'Add slot' once the list reaches the wheel's reported position count, with a tooltip naming the count.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by reading the named file; not driven live because re-entering onboarding would have wiped the profile the other verifications depend on. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/onboarding/steps/filter_wheel_step.dart:268-275: onPressed: (_loadingSlots || _controllers.length >= 12) ? null : _addSlot -- the only cap is a hardcoded 12, never the wheel's reported position count, even though _seedSlotsFromDevice has just read that count from the device ('so the editor reflects the hardware (e.g. 8 slots), not a hardcoded default'). So on a 7-position wheel the button stays enabled and creates rows 8..12. The renumbering sub-claim also holds structurally: slot labels are '${i + 1}' from List.generate(_controllers.length, ...) (lines 282-295), so deleting a middle slot shifts every label below it, which silently re-maps per-filter focus offsets. Severity P3 stands.
